claim: Electron cryo-tomography (cryoET) was used to present the structure of procentrioles from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
source: Using electron cryo-tomography (cryoET) we present the structure of procentrioles from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the method used and the organism studied.

claim: A set of non-tubulin components are attached to the triplet microtubule (MT).
source: We identified a set of non-tubulin components attached to the triplet microtubule (MT), many are at the junctions of tubules likely to reinforce the triplet.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from the structural analysis.

claim: Many non-tubulin components are at the junctions of tubules and likely reinforce the triplet.
source: We identified a set of non-tubulin components attached to the triplet microtubule (MT), many are at the junctions of tubules likely to reinforce the triplet.
evidence: The abstract provides both the observation and an interpretation of function.

claim: The structure of the A-C linker that bridges neighboring triplets was described.
source: We describe structure of the A-C linker that bridges neighboring triplets.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this structural finding.

claim: POC1 is likely an integral component of the A-C linker.
source: The structure infers that POC1 is likely an integral component of A-C linker.
evidence: The abstract presents this as an inference from structural data.

claim: POC1's conserved WD40 β-propeller domain provides attachment sites for other A-C linker components.
source: Its conserved WD40 β-propeller domain provides attachment sites for other A-C linker components.
evidence: The abstract states this functional interpretation based on structural features.

claim: The twist of the A-C linker results in an iris diaphragm-like motion of the triplets in the longitudinal direction of procentriole.
source: The twist of A-C linker results in an iris diaphragm-like motion of the triplets in the longitudinal direction of procentriole.
evidence: The abstract describes this structural dynamic observation.

claim: Two assembly intermediates were identified at the growing ends of procentriole.
source: Finally, we identified two assembly intermediates at the growing ends of procentriole allowing us to propose a model for the procentriole assembly.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding.

claim: The centriole is a barrel-shaped structure composed of a set of MT triplets arranged in nine-fold symmetry.
source: The centriole is a barrel-shaped structure composed of a set of MT triplets arranged in a characteristic nine-fold symmetry.
evidence: The introduction provides this established structural description.

claim: The centriole is an evolutionarily conserved organelle.
source: As an evolutionarily conserved organelle, the centriole, also known as the basal body, fulfills many cellular functions.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: In cycling cells, a pair of centrioles recruits pericentriolar material (PCM) to form the centrosome.
source: In cycling cells, a pair of centrioles recruits pericentriolar material (PCM). Together they form the centrosome, the primary microtubule organizing center (MTOC) in animal cells.
evidence: The introduction describes this established cellular process.

claim: The centrosome is the primary microtubule organizing center (MTOC) in animal cells.
source: Together they form the centrosome, the primary microtubule organizing center (MTOC) in animal cells.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: The centrosome is essential for mitotic spindle formation, spindle orientation and faithful mitotic chromosome segregation.
source: Related to its function as an MTOC, the centrosome is essential for mitotic spindle formation, spindle orientation and faithful mitotic chromosome segregation and for intracellular transport of cargoes.
evidence: The introduction describes established functions of the centrosome.

claim: In non-dividing cells, the centriole functions as basal body to template cilium formation.
source: In non-dividing cells, the centriole functions as basal body to template cilium formation.
evidence: The introduction states this established function.

claim: Mutations affecting centrioles and basal bodies cause diverse human diseases, ranging from tumors to different forms of ciliopathies.
source: Given the array of diverse functions carried out by centrioles and basal bodies, it is not surprising that mutations affecting centrioles and basal bodies cause diverse human diseases, ranging from tumors to different forms of ciliopathies (Nigg and Raff, 2009; Reiter and Leroux, 2017)
evidence: The introduction cites literature supporting this claim about disease associations.

claim: Centriole biogenesis is tightly controlled.
source: Centriole biogenesis is tightly controlled.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: Centriole biogenesis occurs by a cascade of molecular events performed by evolutionarily conserved components.
source: Genetics and cell biological studies in various model organisms show that centriole biogenesis occurs by a cascade of molecular events performed by evolutionarily conserved components, reviewed by Banterle and Gönczy (2017).
evidence: The introduction cites a review supporting this claim.

claim: In vertebrate cells, the nine-fold symmetric structure called the cartwheel forms at the proximal side of the mature centriole.
source: First, the nine-fold symmetric structure called the cartwheel forms at the proximal side of the mature centriole (mother centriole).
evidence: The introduction describes this as an established step in centriole assembly.

claim: MT triplets assemble at the tip of the nine radial spokes in the cartwheel.
source: This is followed by assembly of MT triplets at the tip of the nine radial spokes in the cartwheel.
evidence: The introduction describes this sequential assembly step.

claim: The cartwheel and MT triplets together form the procentriole, a precursor of the daughter centriole.
source: Together, they form the procentriole, a precursor of the daughter centriole.
evidence: The introduction defines the procentriole based on established knowledge.

claim: During mitosis, the mother and daughter centrioles are 'disengaged' but remain loosely linked.
source: During mitosis, the mother and daughter centrioles are 'disengaged' but remain loosely linked.
evidence: The introduction describes this established process in the centriole cycle.

claim: The centriole duplication process in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is tightly controlled.
source: Similar to the centriole duplication in metazoans such as in mammals, the centriole duplication process in the unicellular organism Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is tightly controlled.
evidence: The introduction states this based on cited studies.

claim: The centriole duplication process in Chlamydomonas has been described in a series of seminal studies.
source: The process has been described in a series of seminal studies (Cavalier-Smith, 1974; Geimer and Melkonian, 2004; O'Toole and Dutcher, 2014).
evidence: The introduction cites specific studies describing the process.

claim: A number of key components in Chlamydomonas centriole assembly have been found conserved in other organisms.
source: Compared to the vertebrates, despite many morphological and ultrastructural differences in the duplication steps, a number of key components in the Chlamydomonas centriole assembly have been found conserved in other organisms (Dutcher et al., 2002; Dutcher and Trabuco, 1998; Hiraki et al., 2007; Keller et al., 2009; Matsuura et al., 2004; Nakazawa et al., 2007).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple studies supporting conservation of components.

claim: Proteomics and bioinformatics studies have identified a list of major structural components of centrioles.
source: In addition, proteomics and bioinformatics studies in several model organisms have identified a list of major structural components of centrioles (Andersen et al., 2003; Keller et al., 2005; Kilburn et al., 2007; Li et al., 2004; Müller et al., 2010).
evidence: The introduction cites studies that identified centriole components.

claim: The centriole is assembled by a series of evolutionarily conserved protein building blocks.
source: Together, these studies concur that the centriole is assembled by a series of evolutionarily conserved protein building blocks.
evidence: The introduction synthesizes findings from cited studies.

claim: The centriole assembly process is tightly controlled spatially and temporally by a set of regulatory proteins.
source: The process is tightly controlled spatially and temporally by a set of regulatory proteins (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2010; Hodges et al., 2010).
evidence: The introduction cites studies supporting this regulatory mechanism.

claim: Several crystal structures are available describing components of the centriole, including Plk4, Spd2, Sas6, Cep135, STIL and CPAP.
source: Several crystal structures are now available describing components of the centriole, including Plk4, Spd2, Sas6, Cep135, STIL and CPAP.
evidence: The introduction states this as established structural knowledge.

claim: There have been cryoET studies on assembly of centriole in several organisms.
source: In addition, there have been cryoET studies on assembly of centriole in several organisms (Greenan et al., 2018; Guichard et al., 2010; Guichard et al., 2012; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction cites cryoET studies on centriole assembly.

claim: The events of cartwheel assembly have been studied extensively.
source: In particular, the events of cartwheel assembly has been studied extensively (Guichard et al., 2012; Guichard et al., 2017; Hilbert et al., 2016; Kitagawa et al., 2011; van Breugel et al., 2011), leading to a molecular mechanism that at least in part establishes the 9-fold symmetry, reviewed in (Guichard et al., 2018).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple studies and a review on cartwheel assembly.

claim: A complete picture of the centriole architecture and its assembly mechanism is lacking.
source: Despite the structural and functional study of many centriole components in the past years, a complete picture of the centriole architecture and its assembly mechanism is lacking.
evidence: The introduction identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: 11 non-tubulin components were identified in the structure that are associated with the triplet tubules in an asymmetric manner.
source: We identify 11 non-tubulin components in the structure that are associated with the triplet tubules in an asymmetric manner.
evidence: The results section states this finding from the structural analysis.

claim: The nuclear-flagellar-apparatus (NFAp) from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii were isolated and visualized by cryoET.
source: To study the structure of both the centriole and procentriole, the nuclear-flagellar-apparatus (NFAp) from the unicellular green algae Chlamydomonas reinhardtii were isolated and visualized by cryoET.
evidence: The results section describes the experimental approach.

claim: The collected tilt series and reconstructed tomograms show good conservation of the stereotypical structures of NFAp.
source: The collected tilt series and the reconstructed tomograms show good conservation of the stereotypical structures of NFAp (Video 1).
evidence: The results section describes observations from tomograms and references a video.

claim: In many tomograms, two well-preserved procentrioles are attached to their respective mother centrioles via the rMT.
source: In many tomograms, two well-preserved procentrioles are attached to their respective mother centrioles via the rMT (Figure 1B, Video 1).
evidence: The results section describes observations from tomograms with figure and video references.

claim: An averaged structure of MT triplet was obtained at 23.0 Å resolution using subtomogram averaging.
source: Using subtomogram averaging, we obtained an averaged structure of MT triplet at 23.0 Å resolution (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section states the resolution achieved with figure references.

claim: All MT protofilaments (PF) can be resolved in the triplet structure, as well as the 4 nm repeat of tubulin along the PF.
source: In this structure, all MT protofilaments (PF) can be resolved, as well as the 4 nm repeat of tubulin along the PF.
evidence: The results section describes the level of detail visible in the structure.

claim: The A-tubule is composed of 13 PFs as an elliptical ring deviated from the canonical MT structure.
source: This confirms previous observations from the central core region and from centrioles in other organisms that the A-tubule is composed of 13 PFs as an elliptical ring deviated from the canonical MT structure.
evidence: The results section confirms this structural feature with reference to previous observations.

claim: Both B- and C-tubules are partial rings with 10 PFs.
source: Both B- and C-tubules are partial rings with 10 PFs.
evidence: The results section describes this structural feature.

claim: The pinhead is a structure that connects the A-tubule to the cartwheel.
source: These include the pinhead, a structure that connects the A-tubule to the cartwheel, and the A-C linker that bridges A-tubule to the C-tubule of its neighboring triplet.
evidence: The results section describes the function of the pinhead.

claim: The A-C linker bridges A-tubule to the C-tubule of its neighboring triplet.
source: These include the pinhead, a structure that connects the A-tubule to the cartwheel, and the A-C linker that bridges A-tubule to the C-tubule of its neighboring triplet.
evidence: The results section describes the function of the A-C linker.

claim: Without imposing symmetry, the pinhead is about 70 nm away from the central hub.
source: In the model, without imposing symmetry, the pinhead is about 70 nm away from the central hub.
evidence: The results section provides a measurement from the model.

claim: The A-C linker makes multiple connections to both the neighboring A- and C-tubules.
source: The A-C linker is clearly visible and makes multiple connections to both the neighboring A- and C-tubules, although with blurred details compared to the MTs in the triplet, indicating structural heterogeneity and flexibility in this region.
evidence: The results section describes observations from the model.

claim: The A-C linker shows structural heterogeneity and flexibility.
source: The A-C linker is clearly visible and makes multiple connections to both the neighboring A- and C-tubules, although with blurred details compared to the MTs in the triplet, indicating structural heterogeneity and flexibility in this region.
evidence: The results section infers heterogeneity and flexibility from blurred details.

claim: There are notable differences between the triplet averages from the proximal region of mother centrioles and from procentrioles.
source: Even though the MT backbones are nearly identical, there are notable differences between these two averages.
evidence: The results section compares two datasets and identifies differences.

claim: A number of microtubule inner proteins (MIPs) attached to the centriole B-tubule are absent in the procentriole triplet.
source: A number of microtubule inner proteins (MIPs) that are attached to the centriole B-tubule, in particular MIPs present in the inner junction of A-B and B-C tubule, are absent in the procentriole triplet.
evidence: The results section identifies differences between centriole and procentriole structures.

claim: Some luminal densities in the procentriole are missing in the centriole.
source: Conversely, some luminal densities in the procentriole are missing in the centriole.
evidence: The results section identifies differences between structures.

claim: A 'focused refinement' strategy was applied to align the A-, B- and C-tubules of the triplet separately.
source: To improve resolution, we applied a 'focused refinement' strategy widely used in single particle cryoEM (Scheres, 2016), to align the A-, B- and C-tubules of the triplet separately.
evidence: The results section describes the image processing method used.

claim: Focused refinement resulted in three averaged tubule structures at 21.4 Å, 22.3 Å and 22.3 Å resolution for A-, B- and C-tubules respectively.
source: These resulted in three averaged tubule structures, with improved resolution at 21.4 Å, 22.3 Å and 22.3 Å, respectively (Figure 2A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section reports the resolutions achieved with figure references.

claim: A total of 11 MIPs were identified associated with the MT wall.
source: Based on the improved structures, we built a MT model for each tubule, allowing us to identify a total of 11 MIPs associated with the MT wall (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–11).
evidence: The results section states the number of MIPs identified with figure references.

claim: MIP1 and MIP2 share similar binding pattern as the MIPs previously seen in the core region.
source: Among them, two components MIP1 and MIP2 share similar binding pattern as the MIPs previously seen in the core region (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: The results section compares findings to a previous study.

claim: MIP1 is a cone-shaped structure projecting from PF A5 into the lumen of the A-tubule with an 8 nm longitudinal periodicity.
source: MIP1 is a cone-shaped structure projecting from PF A5 into the lumen of the A-tubule and having an 8 nm longitudinal periodicity.
evidence: The results section describes the structure and periodicity of MIP1.

claim: Each MIP1 has two legs that recognize the luminal side of α/β tubulin dimer.
source: Each MIP1 has two legs that recognize the luminal side of α/β tubulin dimer (arrowheads in Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section describes the binding mode of MIP1 with figure reference.

claim: MIP2 is more filamentous, forming a trellis-like meshwork, laterally spanning PFs A11 to A13.
source: By contrast, MIP2 is more filamentous, forming a trellis-like meshwork, laterally spanning PFs A11 to A13.
evidence: The results section describes the structure of MIP2.

claim: MIP2 follows the pitch of the 3-start helical MT lattice running along the A-tubule luminal wall.
source: It follows the pitch of the 3-start helical MT lattice running along the A-tubule luminal wall (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), presumably to reinforce the 'ribbon' structure that is shared by the A- and B-tubules.
evidence: The results section describes the arrangement of MIP2 with figure reference and functional inference.

claim: 7 of the 11 MIPs (MIPs 3 ~ 6, MIPs 9 ~ 11) are localized at or in the vicinity of the inner junctions of the A-B or B-C tubules.
source: Of interest, 7 of the 11 MIPs (MIPs 3 ~ 6, MIPs 9 ~ 11) are localized at or in the vicinity of the inner junctions of the A-B or B-C tubules.
evidence: The results section identifies the localization pattern of specific MIPs.

claim: MIP9 at the inner B-C tubule junction forms a filament exhibiting 4 nm periodicity.
source: Among them, the MIP9 at the inner B-C tubule junction, is of particular interest. Even though it forms a filament exhibiting 4 nm periodicity, the structure deviates from a canonical MT protofilament (Figure 2—figure supplement 12).
evidence: The results section describes the structure of MIP9 with figure reference.

claim: MIP9 structure deviates from a canonical MT protofilament.
source: Even though it forms a filament exhibiting 4 nm periodicity, the structure deviates from a canonical MT protofilament (Figure 2—figure supplement 12). Therefore, we assigned it as a non-tubulin protein MIP9.
evidence: The results section compares MIP9 to canonical MT structure with figure reference.

claim: Inner junction MIPs crosslink multiple PFs forming intricate networks.
source: Together, these inner junctions MIPs crosslink multiple PFs forming intricate networks.
evidence: The results section describes the structural arrangement of MIPs.

claim: Inner junction MIPs are likely important in strengthening the overall triplet structure.
source: They are likely important in strengthening the overall triplet structure.
evidence: The results section infers a functional role for the MIPs.

claim: The pinhead can be partitioned into three parts: pinbody (PinB), pinfoot 1 (PinF1) and pinfoot 2 (PinF2).
source: Consistent with a previous study (Guichard et al., 2013), the pinhead can be partitioned into three parts, namely pinbody (PinB), pinfoot 1 (PinF1) and pinfoot 2 (PinF2) where both pinfeet attach to the MT wall.
evidence: The results section describes the pinhead structure consistent with a cited study.

claim: Each PinF1/PinF2 unit forms a ring structure bound to α/β tubulin dimer on PF A3.
source: Each PinF1/PinF2 unit forms a ring structure bound to α/β tubulin dimer on PF A3, therefore, the entire pinhead repeats every 8 nm.
evidence: The results section describes the binding mode and periodicity of the pinhead.

claim: The entire pinhead repeats every 8 nm.
source: Each PinF1/PinF2 unit forms a ring structure bound to α/β tubulin dimer on PF A3, therefore, the entire pinhead repeats every 8 nm.
evidence: The results section states the periodicity of the pinhead.

claim: The 8 nm periodicity of the pinhead is in agreement with a recent triplet structure from the proximal region of mammalian centriole.
source: This is in agreement with a recent triplet structure from the proximal region of mammalian centriole (Greenan et al., 2018).
evidence: The results section compares findings to a cited study.

claim: The PinB turns 90 degree from the pinfeet, forming an inverted L-shaped structure.
source: The PinB turns 90 degree from the pinfeet, forming an inverted L-shaped structure (Figure 2D).
evidence: The results section describes the structure of PinB with figure reference.

claim: There is a longitudinal gap between neighboring PinB every 8 nm without connection.
source: There is a longitudinal gap between neighboring PinB every 8 nm without connection.
evidence: The results section describes a structural feature of PinB.

claim: The distal tip of PinB is flexible exhibiting less well-defined structure in the average.
source: The distal tip of PinB is flexible exhibiting less well-defined structure in the average (arrowheads in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 14).
evidence: The results section infers flexibility from structural features with figure references.

claim: PFs A2 and A3 display the highest curvature of the MT wall with a large lateral gap between these two PFs.
source: Interestingly, among the 13 PFs that form the elliptical-shaped A-tubule, the PFs A2 and A3 display the highest curvature of the MT wall with a large lateral gap between these two PFs where the MIP4 laterally crosslinks.
evidence: The results section describes a structural feature of the A-tubule.

claim: The high local curvature and gap at PFs A2 and A3 may create a unique site for anchoring the pinhead to the A-tubule.
source: The high local curvature and the gap may create a unique site for anchoring the pinhead to the A-tubule.
evidence: The results section infers a functional significance of the structural feature.

claim: The A-C linker is weaker than the MT triplet in the averaged triplet structure, indicating compositional and/or conformational heterogeneity.
source: In the averaged triplet structure (Figure 1C), the A-C linker is weaker than the MT triplet, indicating either compositional and/or conformational heterogeneity.
evidence: The results section infers heterogeneity from weaker density with figure reference.

claim: Four classes of subtomograms were obtained showing a more complete and detailed structure of the A-C linker associated with the A-tubule.
source: By extensive subtomogram classification and alignment using the A-tubule as a reference (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and detailed in Materials and Methods), we obtained four classes whose averaged structures showing a more complete and detailed structure of the A-C linker most closely associated with the A-tubule (Figure 3—figure supplements 2,3).
evidence: The results section describes the classification results with figure references.

claim: Six classes of subtomograms were identified showing enhanced detail for the portion of the A-C linker associated with the C-tubule.
source: Similarly, in a 'reciprocal classification' by using the C-tubule as the reference point, we identified 6 classes of subtomograms whose averaged structure shows enhanced detail for the portion of the A-C linker associated with the C-tubule (Figure 3—figure supplements 3–5).
evidence: The results section describes the classification results with figure references.

claim: The differences in the A-C linker classes largely reflect the underlying flexibility of the A-C linker about its midpoint.
source: The differences in the classes largely reflect the underlying flexibility of the A-C linker about its midpoint.
evidence: The results section interprets the classification results.

claim: The A-C linker forms a crisscross-shaped structure.
source: Overall, the A-C linker forms a crisscross-shaped structure (Figure 3A, Video 2) that can be divided into five parts: a central trunk region, from which two arms (Arm A, B) and two legs (Leg A, B), extend out to the C- and A-tubules, respectively.
evidence: The results section describes the overall structure with figure and video references.

claim: Arm A forms a longitudinal helical filament with 8 nm periodicity and binds to PF C8 of the C-tubule.
source: Arm A forms a longitudinal helical filament with 8 nm periodicity and binds to PF C8 of the C-tubule (Figure 3B).
evidence: The results section describes the structure and binding of Arm A with figure reference.

claim: Arm B inserts into the trough between PFs C9 and C10 of the C-tubule, likely binding to both PFs.
source: The Arm B inserts into the trough between PFs C9 and C10 of the C-tubule, likely binding to both PFs.
evidence: The results section describes the binding mode of Arm B with inference.

claim: Leg A has a thin rod shape that tilts ~30° towards the proximal end of procentriole and extends about 10 nm to reach and contact PF A6 of A-tubule.
source: The Leg A has a thin rod shape that tilts ~30° towards the proximal end of procentriole and extends about 10 nm to reach and contact PF A6 of A-tubule (Figure 3C).
evidence: The results section describes the structure and dimensions of Leg A with figure reference.

claim: Leg B tilts ~30° towards the distal end of procentriole and spans about 22 nm to connect to both PFs A9 and A10 of the A-tubule.
source: Leg B tilts ~30° towards the distal end of procentriole. It spans about 22 nm to connect to both PFs A9 and A10 of the A-tubule.
evidence: The results section describes the structure and dimensions of Leg B.

claim: Leg B continues to reach as far as to the outer junction of A- and B-tubules.
source: It continues to reach as far as to the outer junction of A- and B-tubules (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The results section describes the extent of Leg B with figure references.

claim: The central trunk can be divided into three longitudinal filaments bundled into a spiral: f1, f2, f3.
source: Lastly, the central trunk can be further divided into three longitudinal filaments bundled into a spiral: f1, f2, f3 (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The results section describes the structure of the central trunk with figure references.

claim: There is a doughnut-shaped density within Leg B with an average diameter of ~4 nm that stacks longitudinally with 8 nm periodicity.
source: Strikingly there is a doughnut-shaped density with the Leg B. The averaged diameter of the ring is ~4 nm and they stack longitudinally with 8 nm periodicity (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The results section describes a structural feature with figure references.

claim: POC1 localizes to the centriole proximal ends.
source: Previous studies found the conserved centriole components, POC1, to localize to the centriole proximal ends (Keller et al., 2009; Pearson et al., 2009b).
evidence: The results section cites studies on POC1 localization.

claim: Knockdown or deletion of POC1 in several organisms resulted in defective centrioles or basal bodies.
source: Knockdown or deletion of POC1 in several organisms resulted in defective centrioles or basal bodies (Khire et al., 2016; Pearson et al., 2009a; Venoux et al., 2013).
evidence: The results section cites studies on POC1 function.

claim: Human mutations of either POC1A or POC1B cause ciliopathy-like pathologies.
source: Human mutations of either paralog, POC1A or POC1B, cause ciliopathy-like pathologies (Beck et al., 2014; Roosing et al., 2014; Sarig et al., 2012; Shaheen et al., 2012).
evidence: The results section cites studies on POC1 mutations and disease.

claim: In Tetrahymena, POC1 is important for maintaining A-C linker integrity.
source: In Tetrahymena, POC1 is important for maintaining A-C linker integrity.
evidence: The results section states this functional role.

claim: poc1 null mutants in Tetrahymena display basal body defects ranging from missing or disintegrated triplets to disconnected neighboring triplets and aberrant A-C linkers.
source: poc1 null mutants display basal body defects ranging from missing or disintegrated triplets to disconnected neighboring triplets and aberrant A-C linkers (Meehl et al., 2016; Pearson et al., 2009a).
evidence: The results section cites studies on poc1 mutant phenotypes.

claim: One of the predicted conserved signatures of POC1 is multiple WD40 repeats at its N-terminus.
source: Interestingly, one of predicted conserved signatures of POC1 is multiple WD40 repeats at its N-terminus (Woodland and Fry, 2008), for example, in Chlamydomonas, POC1 is predicted to have seven tandem WD40 repeats at its N-terminus (Keller et al., 2009).
evidence: The results section cites studies on POC1 sequence features.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, POC1 is predicted to have seven tandem WD40 repeats at its N-terminus.
source: for example, in Chlamydomonas, POC1 is predicted to have seven tandem WD40 repeats at its N-terminus (Keller et al., 2009).
evidence: The results section cites a study on Chlamydomonas POC1 structure.

claim: A crystal structure of a 7-repeat WD40 β-propeller domain fits remarkably well into the ring density observed on Leg B.
source: A crystal structure of a 7-repeat WD40 β-propeller domain fits remarkably well into the ring density observed on the Leg B (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: The results section describes model fitting with figure references.

claim: In the docked model, the WD40 β-propeller makes multiple contacts with the rest of Leg B.
source: Nevertheless, in the docked model, the WD40 β-propeller makes multiple contacts with the rest of Leg B, consistent with the function of WD40 domain as one of the most abundant protein-protein interaction domains that scaffolds multi-protein complexes (Stirnimann et al., 2010).
evidence: The results section describes the model and cites knowledge about WD40 domains.

claim: Human ciliopathy mutations in POC1A or POC1B map to the WD40 repeats.
source: Notably, human ciliopathy mutations in POC1A or POC1B map to the WD40 repeats.
evidence: The results section states this observation about mutation locations.

claim: POC1 has also been found at other locations in mother centriole and in flagellum.
source: However, in addition to procentriole, POC1 has also been found at other locations in mother centriole and in flagellum (Keller et al., 2009; Pearson et al., 2009b).
evidence: The results section cites studies on POC1 localization.

claim: Analysis of the A-C linker heterogeneity led to the identification of 4 and 6 conformational classes in two classification schemes.
source: As discussed above, analysis of the A-C linker heterogeneity led to the identification of 4 and 6 conformational classes in two classification schemes where either the A- or C-tubule was used as a reference point (Figure 3—figure supplements 1,4).
evidence: The results section describes the classification analysis with figure references.

claim: Overlaying projections from the A-C linker classes reveals a large and continuous swinging motion of the linker relative to the reference point.
source: Overlaying projections from these classes, in both schemes, reveals a large and continuous swinging motion of the remaining portion of the linker relative to the reference point (Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: The results section describes observations from overlays with video references.

claim: The swing angle θ changes up to 10 or 16 degrees respectively in two classification schemes.
source: The swing angle θ (Figure 4A, Table 2) changes up to 10 or 16 degrees respectively in two schemes.
evidence: The results section reports measurements with figure and table references.

claim: Two neighboring triplets twist progressively along the procentriole in a left-handed manner with the thumb pointing towards the MT plus end.
source: Since the proximal region of the mother centriole has a defined length, calculating the weighted average of the swing angle at each longitudinal position along the triplet (Figure 4B,C) shows that two neighboring triplets, by using the A-C linker as a pivot point, twist progressively along the procentriole in a left-handed manner with the thumb pointing towards the MT plus end, as illustrated in Figure 4A.
evidence: The results section describes the twist motion with figure references.

claim: The central trunk region of the A-C linker is at the pivot point of the twist motion.
source: The overlays clearly show the central trunk region of the A-C linker is at the pivot point of this twist motion (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: The results section describes observations from overlays with figure references.

claim: The trunk is composed of a bundle of 3 inter-connected filaments (f1, f2 and f3) that form a spiral.
source: Interestingly, the trunk is composed of a bundle of 3 inter-connected filaments, f1, f2 and f3 (Figure 3A–C). Together they form a spiral that likely drives, at least in part, the twist motion of neighboring triplets.
